history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. Popularly called the Sheeshe Wala (glass) Gurudwara, its proper name is Gurudwara Sri Sangat Sar Sahib, in village Rajgarh near Doraha, about 22 km from Ludhiana on NH 44. Its claim to fame is that the floors, walls, ceiling and even the fans are made of glass and mirror work, lit with coloured lights. The CSV town is 'Ludhiana'; the actual site is the village of Rajgarh (near Doraha), Ludhiana district — town corrected. Photography and video are not allowed inside the sanctum.

name: Sheeshe Wala Gurudwara
town_description: Rajgarh is a village in Doraha tehsil of Ludhiana district, Punjab, about 6 km from Doraha town and 22 km from Ludhiana city on the Ludhiana-Doraha road (NH 44). It is known for the glass-clad Gurudwara Sri Sangat Sar Sahib, which draws Sikh pilgrims and tourists from across the region.
